_blasts: A grenade going off, felt (main.ts, impacts.ts, audio.ts). Ours, after Apex and Warzone: within shakeRadius metres the view shakes by up to shakeDeg degrees, falling off with the square of the distance and dying away over shakeTime seconds (the screen-shake setting scales it, and Off turns it off); within ringRadius metres your ears ring for ringTime seconds, the world muffled to ringHz; a column of smokes grey sprites rises for smokeTime seconds, and a scorch scorchSize metres across stays on the ground as long as a bullet hole.
_tracers: Tracers (projectile.ts). Ours, after Apex and Warzone: a streak along the round's flight, a frame's travel long up to maxLen metres, width metres across and never thinner than minPx on screen; drawn from the gun's muzzle and joined to the real path (which leaves the eye) over the first blend metres.
_impacts: Bullet impacts on the level (src/game/impacts.ts). Ours: holes is how many hole decals stay on the map at once (the oldest goes first), each holeSize metres across and gone after holeLife seconds; a hit throws puffPer dust sprites (sparks off metal) from a pool of puffs, each living puffLife seconds; the sound carries hearing metres.
_killMarker: The knock and kill marker (hud.ts hitMarker). Ours, after Valorant's and Apex's: a knock is orange and a kill red, scale times the size of a hit's marker, held for hold seconds against a hit's 0.12; the chime under a kill climbs by chimeStep semitones for each kill within streak seconds of the last, up to chimeMax steps.
_lowAmmo: The low-ammo warning. Ours, after Apex and Warzone: at warn of the magazine or less the count turns amber and LOW AMMO shows under the crosshair, at none it reads RELOAD in red; over the last click of the magazine each shot adds a dry click rising in pitch as it runs out. A magazine under minClip rounds (a sniper, a shotgun) is short by design and gets neither.
_damageNumbers: Damage numbers. Ours, after Apex's default: every hit on the same target within stack seconds of the last adds to one number, which pops to 1.25 times its size and back over pop seconds as it grows; a spray used to draw one number a round, sixteen of them on top of each other.
_muzzleFlash: Other players' muzzle flashes (src/game/muzzle.ts). Ours: a flash lights for life seconds on each shot, two frames at 60 fps, as a player's own view model flash does; size is its width in metres up close, a little over a rifle's muzzle brake; minPx is the fewest pixels across it is ever drawn on screen, so a shot at 150 m is still a point of light and not nothing.
_scopeGlint: A scoped figure's lens flare (muzzle.ts fitGlint), Hyper Scape's patch 1.1: "a Lens Flare when players are aiming with the rifle, to give warning to their potential victims". On a figure aimed in (its aim past `from`) holding a gun with a magnified optic, at the front of the gun's sight line: `size` metres across, never under `minPx` pixels on screen (its players found Hyper Scape's "too big, covering the entire body", so ours is about a head's width near (0.12 m read as a few pixels at 6 m, lost against the gun's white skin) and never under a clear star far), in `color`, a cool white, twinkling by `twinkle` of itself; its streak across is four times its height.
_hsCharge: BOOG's recharge in its Hyper Scape scope (hud.ts drawHsScope): after a shot a ring `radius` of the screen's height round the aim point, `width` pixels thick at 1080p, closing clockwise from the top in `fill` over its `track` as the gun recharges, `charging` under it; when it can fire again the ring and `readyText` flash in `ready` and fade over `flash` s. Where the eye already is, so it is read without looking away (the owner, 2026-09-27: "when the user can shoot again, I thought we agreed on having a bar there"); it had been a 90 by 4 pixel bar at the frame's left edge. Ours. The owner, 2026-09-27: half see-through, and no READY ("they know it's ready when the circle is done"): `fill` at 0.5, `track` at 0.11, `flash` 0 (none).
_trails: Movement trails behind every other player (src/game/trails.ts), Hyper Scape's: red behind enemies, blue behind mates, gold behind the crown's carrier. A ribbon `width` metres across, `lift` over the feet, a point every `step` metres the feet go, at most `points` of them, each fading over `seconds` (its players saw a trail linger 0.5 to 1 s after someone went invisible); a jump of more than `jump` metres between frames (a respawn, a DASH) starts it afresh; none past `maxDist` metres. Colours read off Hyper Scape's footage, by eye. The owner, 2026-09-27, of the "red circle/bubble" round enemies that made them hard to track: it was these. A bot dodging side to side in a fight laid its trail back and forth under its feet, a bright red zigzag smeared round the figure (a picture of one 8 m off, dodging 1.4 m). So a trail is laid only while the feet go `minSpeed` m/s or more (running; SpeedKills runs at 8.8 and sprints at 14), a turn back on itself (the way on against the way before below `turnBack`, a dot product) starts it afresh, it is `opacity` as bright, and it fades out as its player comes nearer than `near` metres (gone at the first, whole at the second), where the eye is on the figure itself.
_note: The HUD's few gameplay numbers (ours). Plates: an enemy's name and bars show only after you have damaged them, for `afterHit` seconds from the last hit, and only while the line from your eye to their chest is clear of the level; a team mate's always. A plate is last drawn at `range` metres, fading from `fadeFrom`: the owner asked for them off far away as well as behind cover, so this is a room-and-a-half, not the width of the map.
_loot: Looting, so that kitting up after a landing is not dozens of presses with your head down (ours; Apex, Warzone and The Finals all take ammo as you walk over it and let you hold one key to empty a box). `reach` is the radius round your feet the prompt's list covers, wider than loot.json's 2.2 m aimed reach so a whole spot fits in one list, and `floorGap` keeps that list to the floor you are standing on now that the buildings hold loot upstairs. `sweep` is the walk-over radius: an item whose kind is in `autoKinds` and, for a heal, whose id is in `autoHeals`, comes up inside it with no press at all. `startAfter` is how long the key must stay down before the hold starts emptying the spot, so a tap still takes exactly one thing; `cadence` is the gap between the ones after that, slow enough to read the notices and fast enough to clear a death box in a second. `askAgain` stops a guest asking the host for the same item every frame while the answer is still in flight. `listMax` is how many rows the list shows, and `cycle` is the action that steps it: the armour cycle, a range tool with nothing to do in a battle royale, so it is free to borrow here.
_swapGuard: loot.swapGuard: seconds after you take a gun during which a gun that appears within reach is left out of the list. Taking a gun with both slots full puts the one in hand down at your feet, inside the reach list, and nearest. A press read over several frames, or a hold, took it straight back and put the new one down, and the two swapped every frame for as long as the key was down. Ours: long enough to cover a press and let go, short enough that a gun dropped by someone else a moment later is still offered.
_boxClear: loot.boxClear: metres round a death box inside which the walk-over pickup takes nothing. A box's things are spread 0.9 m round it (brmatch.ts dropBox), so 1.6 covers them with a margin. Without it a squad mate respawning the owner at the box swept up the ammo and heals the owner was meant to get back. Ours.
_damageDir: Where you are being shot from: a red arc round the crosshair pointing at whoever hit you, the way Apex, Warzone and every other shooter since Halo draws it. Without it a hit from behind was a number going down and no idea which way to turn. life is how long an arc lasts after the last hit from that direction, radius and thick its size in HUD pixels at 1080p, arc its width in degrees. A new hit from within merge metres of an arc's source refreshes that arc instead of stacking a second one, and at most max are shown, newest first. Ours.
_reticle: The crosshair's options (Settings, Crosshair; src/game/reticle.ts). The default is the crosshair the game always had, Apex's three prongs and a dot, white, dynamic with the gun's spread, so nobody sees a change until they ask for one. The colours are the ones every competitive shooter offers, and they are chosen to stay apart for the three common kinds of colour blindness: the green and the magenta, and the yellow and the cyan, are the pairs to use when red and green look alike. limits are the ranges the settings accept; a stored value outside them is clamped. Ours.
_summary: The match summary: the card over the middle of the screen when a match ends, with the result, your numbers, the XP it paid and the level bar filling. show is how long it stays, seconds; fill is how long the level bar takes to run from where you were to where you are, which is the moment the XP reads as earned rather than as a number. A new match starting takes it down at once. Ours.
_accessibility: Settings, Accessibility (src/game/palette.ts). vision is the set of meaning colours per kind of colour vision: enemy and ally, the softer pair the kill feed uses for its lines, and the damage arcs as r,g,b. Red against green is the pair about one man in twelve cannot tell apart, so the two red-green modes move the enemy to orange and your side to blue, and the blue-yellow mode keeps red but moves your side to a teal that stays clear of it. The normal set is the colours the HUD always used. scales are the HUD sizes offered; a free number is not accepted, because a HUD scaled to 4 is off the screen. Ours, after the palettes Valorant, Apex and Fortnite ship.
_quickChat: Quick chat: the chat key opens these lines and 1 to 6 sends one to everyone in the match, where it shows in the kill feed with your name. A browser game has no text chat worth the name while you are aiming, and playing with a friend with no way to say GG or wait was the gap. open is how long the list stays up untouched, seconds; gap is the least time between two lines, so a key held down or mashed is not a flood. A line travels as its number, so a guest's text never reaches anyone: nobody can type into anyone else's screen. Ours.
_loading: The loading screen (src/ui/loading.ts): up for at least minSeconds so it does not flash, gone once everything asked for is in and a frame is drawn, or after maxSeconds whatever happens. With nothing asked for at all (a page served from the cache) it goes after quietSeconds. A tip turns over every tipSeconds. Ours.

tips: Look straight down in the drop to dive fast, level to glide far.
In a squad the host is the jumpmaster. Press C to break off and fly yourself.
A Ring Console shows your whole squad where the ring goes after next.
Resurgence: every kill by your side takes 5 s off a dead squad mate's wait.
Hold the interact key over a pile of loot to take everything at your feet.
Crouch while you sprint to slide, and jump out of the slide to keep its speed.
M opens the map. The middle mouse button pings a place, an item or an enemy for your squad.
The Mast at the hub is seven floors to the best loot on the map, and everyone knows it.
Walk into a place and its name comes up. The quieter corners are walled compounds.
loading._tipsSk: SpeedKills' tips: what a first-timer needs, a line at a time (the brief: teach only what is necessary).
tipsSk: Double jump, run along walls and climb anything: the roofs are yours.
A second copy of your gun fuses into it: up to level 5.
Pick one mobility hack and one utility hack before the match. Find more on the floor.
The middle of the city is the hottest drop: the most loot, and the most fights.
Sectors of the city decay in waves. Watch the map and keep moving.
Die once and you win your way back in a 1v1. Die again and you are a ghost: stay with your squad to be revived faster.
Hold the capture zone in the last sector to win, or be the last squad standing.
You never run out of ammo. Reload and keep moving.

_layouts: SpeedKills' bottom HUD (Phase 20 A6; src/game/hud.ts drawVitalsSk, drawHacksSk, drawWeaponsSk), in HUD pixels at 1080p times the HUD scale, and times a fit factor when the two sides would meet on a narrow screen. The owner's ask: everything on the bottom edge; the health bar twice the legacy 12 thick and a little longer than 330; the two hacks right of the health, lower and further right than the legacy square at 384, H-134, and bigger than its 58; the ammo count at 88, 1.52 times the legacy 58; the two guns with their fusion pips and level left of the count, digitsBox leaving room for a three-digit magazine; and a dark outline under every text and round every bar (text: lineWidth is the font size times text, kept between min and max; bars: bar). Legacy sizes measured off the live HUD at 1920x1080 by the Phase 20 diagnosis. Ours. The slots are 300 wide and carry the gun's class after its name in kindFont (Phase 20 A7).

speedkills._squad: The squad panel (Phase 27): a row a teammate, stacked up from `gap` over your own speed line, bordered in their colour (`border`) with their number on a square of it (`badge`). Each row is the name, then the shield's segments and the health bar, as your own are drawn below it but smaller, or what has happened to them in their place. `mine` is your own number beside your health, in the margin left of it.

_lootCard: SpeedKills' loot card (Phase 20 A8; src/game/lootcard.ts, hud.ts drawLootCard): what a floor gun or hack core is, what taking it does and how it compares with what you carry. Full, the default, teaches a new player; Compact keeps the verdict and the numbers that decide a swap. ttkHit is the share of rounds on the body the time to kill assumes, against the game's health and shield at close range, reloads counted (the number tools/checks/ttk.ts measures the roster with); same is the ratio band inside which two numbers count as equal (no arrow); hideAds is how far aimed in the card steps aside; w is its width, in HUD pixels at 1080p. Ours.
_wallRun: While you run a wall (hud.ts drawWallRun): a glow `width` of the screen wide at the wall's edge, at most `alpha`, and `streaks` lines sliding down it `speed` screens a second, all as strong as the view's lean off the wall (player.json feel wallRoll), in `color`: the owner, 2026-09-28, 'some sort of visual feedback that we are indeed wallrunning, like empulse does'.
